```ts
    if (ids.length === 0) return new Set();
    const rows = await tx
      .select({ id: products.id })
      .from(products)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(products.tenantId, getTenantId()),
          inArray(products.id, ids),
          eq(products.type, 'goods'),
        ),
      );
    return new Set(rows.map((row) => row.id));
  }

  private async branchOf(tx: Transaction, warehouseId: string): Promise<string> {
    const branchId = (await this.branchesOf(tx, [warehouseId])).get(warehouseId);
    if (branchId === undefined) throw new Error(`Warehouse ${warehouseId} has no branch`);
    return branchId;
  }

  private async branchesOf(
    tx: Transaction,
    warehouseIds: readonly string[],
  ): Promise<Map<string, string>> {
    const ids = [...new Set(warehouseIds)];
    if (ids.length === 0) return new Map();
    const rows = await tx
      .select({ id: warehouses.id, branchId: warehouses.branchId })
      .from(warehouses)
      .where(and(eq(warehouses.tenantId, getTenantId()), inArray(warehouses.id, ids)));
    return new Map(rows.map((row) => [row.id, row.branchId]));
  }

  // FOR UPDATE: every change to a bill takes turns with the others and with an approval (the
  // engine locks it the same way)
  private async lock(tx: Transaction, id: string, version: number): Promise<BillRow> {
    const [row] = await tx
      .select()
      .from(bills)
      .where(and(eq(bills.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(bills.id, id)))
      .for('update');
    if (!row) throw notFound('Bill');
    if (row.version !== version) throw versionConflict();
    return row;
  }

  private async lockDraft(tx: Transaction, id: string, version: number): Promise<BillRow> {
    const row = await this.lock(tx, id, version);
    if (row.status !== 'draft') throw notDraft();
    return row;
  }

  private linesOf(tx: Transaction, billId: string) {
    return tx
      .select()
      .from(billLines)
      .where(and(eq(billLines.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(billLines.billId, billId)))
      .orderBy(asc(billLines.lineNo));
  }

  private expensesOf(tx: Transaction, billId: string) {
    return tx
      .select()
      .from(billExpenses)
      .where(and(eq(billExpenses.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(billExpenses.billId, billId)))
      .orderBy(asc(billExpenses.lineNo));
  }

  private paymentFilter(
    payment: BillPaymentFilter | undefined,
    today: string | null,
  ): SQL | undefined {
    if (payment === 'paid') {
      return sql`${bills.status} = 'posted' AND ${bills.amountPaid} >= ${bills.total}`;
    }
    if (payment === 'open') return isOpen;
    if (payment === 'overdue') return sql`${isOpen} AND ${bills.dueDate} < ${today}::date`;
    return undefined;
  }

  // The workspace's today: a bill is overdue the day after its due date there, not in UTC
  private async today(tx: Transaction): Promise<string> {
    const [settings] = await tx
      .select({ timezone: tenantSettings.timezone })
      .from(tenantSettings)
      .where(eq(tenantSettings.tenantId, getTenantId()));
    return todayIn(settings?.timezone ?? 'Asia/Dhaka');
  }

  private rows(
    tx: Transaction,
    where: SQL | undefined,
    limit: number,
    order: SQL[] = [desc(bills.date), desc(bills.id)],
  ) {
    return tx
      .select({
        bill: bills,
        supplier: { id: parties.id, code: parties.code, name: parties.name },
        lineCount,
      })
      .from(bills)
      .innerJoin(
        parties,
        and(eq(parties.tenantId, bills.tenantId), eq(parties.id, bills.supplierId)),
      )
      .where(and(eq(bills.tenantId, getTenantId()), where))
      .orderBy(...order)
      .limit(limit);
  }

  private async read(tx: Transaction, id: string): Promise<Bill> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    const [found] = await this.rows(tx, eq(bills.id, id), 1);
    if (!found) throw notFound('Bill');
    const { bill: row } = found;
    const lines = await withVariants(tx, await this.linesOf(tx, id));
    const expenses = await this.expensesOf(tx, id);
    const receiptLineIds = lines.flatMap(({ row: line }) =>
      line.receiptLineId === null ? [] : [line.receiptLineId],
    );
    const orderLineIds = lines.flatMap(({ row: line }) =>
      line.orderLineId === null ? [] : [line.orderLineId],
    );
    const [receiptLines, orders, payments] = await Promise.all([
      receiptLineIds.length === 0
        ? []
        : tx
            .select({
              id: goodsReceiptLines.id,
              batchId: goodsReceiptLines.batchId,
              serialNumbers: goodsReceiptLines.serialNumbers,
              orderLineId: goodsReceiptLines.orderLineId,
              value: goodsReceiptLines.value,
              receiptId: goodsReceipts.id,
              number: goodsReceipts.number,
              date: goodsReceipts.date,
            })
            .from(goodsReceiptLines)
            .innerJoin(
              goodsReceipts,
              and(
                eq(goodsReceipts.tenantId, goodsReceiptLines.tenantId),
                eq(goodsReceipts.id, goodsReceiptLines.receiptId),
              ),
            )
            .where(
              and(
                eq(goodsReceiptLines.tenantId, tenantId),
                inArray(goodsReceiptLines.id, receiptLineIds),
              ),
            ),
      orderLineIds.length === 0
        ? []
        : tx
            .select({
              lineId: purchaseOrderLines.id,
              id: purchaseOrders.id,
              number: purchaseOrders.number,
            })
            .from(purchaseOrderLines)
            .innerJoin(
              purchaseOrders,
              and(
                eq(purchaseOrders.tenantId, purchaseOrderLines.tenantId),
                eq(purchaseOrders.id, purchaseOrderLines.orderId),
              ),
            )
            .where(
              and(
                eq(purchaseOrderLines.tenantId, tenantId),
                inArray(purchaseOrderLines.id, orderLineIds),
              ),
            )
            .orderBy(asc(purchaseOrders.number)),
      // Money posted payments applied to it. A draft payment's plan is not money paid (decision
      // 23), and a cancelled one keeps its plan as history: both are left out.
      tx
        .select({
          paymentId: supplierPayments.id,
          paymentNumber: supplierPayments.number,
          date: supplierPayments.date,
          amount: supplierPaymentAllocations.amount,
        })
        .from(supplierPaymentAllocations)
        .innerJoin(
          supplierPayments,
          and(
            eq(supplierPayments.tenantId, supplierPaymentAllocations.tenantId),
            eq(supplierPayments.id, supplierPaymentAllocations.paymentId),
          ),
        )
        .where(
          and(
            eq(supplierPaymentAllocations.tenantId, tenantId),
            eq(supplierPaymentAllocations.billId, id),
            eq(supplierPayments.status, 'posted'),
          ),
        )
        .orderBy(asc(supplierPayments.date), asc(supplierPayments.number)),
    ]);
    const receiptLine = new Map(receiptLines.map((line) => [line.id, line]));
    const batches = await batchesOf(
      tx,
      receiptLines.map((line) => line.batchId),
    );
    const orderOf = new Map(orders.map((order) => [order.lineId, order]));
    const orderRefs = [
      ...new Map(
        orders.map((order) => [order.id, { id: order.id, number: order.number }]),
      ).values(),
    ];
    const receiptRefs = [
      ...new Map(
        receiptLines.map((line) => [
          line.receiptId,
          { id: line.receiptId, number: line.number, date: line.date },
        ]),
      ).values(),
    ].toSorted((a, b) => a.date.localeCompare(b.date) || a.id.localeCompare(b.id));

    const billLinesOut = lines.map(({ row: line, variant }) => {
      const receipt = line.receiptLineId === null ? undefined : receiptLine.get(line.receiptLineId);
      const batch =
        receipt?.batchId === null || receipt === undefined
          ? undefined
          : batches.get(receipt.batchId);
      // The order's price is what a receipt from an order booked; a receipt a bill made has none
      const orderValue =
        receipt !== undefined && receipt.orderLineId !== null ? receipt.value : null;
      return {
        ...toSalesLine(line, variant),
        receiptLineId: line.receiptLineId,
        receiptNumber: receipt?.number ?? null,
        orderLineId: line.orderLineId,
        orderNumber:
          line.orderLineId === null ? null : (orderOf.get(line.orderLineId)?.number ?? null),
        accountId: line.accountId,
        orderValue,
        // What the goods came with: the receipt line's batch once received, else the lot typed on
        // a goods line of its own
        batchId: receipt?.batchId ?? null,
        lotNumber: batch?.lotNumber ?? line.lotNumber,
        expiresOn: batch?.expiresOn ?? line.expiresOn,
        manufacturedOn: batch?.manufacturedOn ?? line.manufacturedOn,
        serialNumbers: receipt?.serialNumbers ?? line.serialNumbers,
      };
    });
    const priceDifference = sumMoney(
      billLinesOut.map((line) => priceDifferenceOf({ net: line.net, orderValue: line.orderValue })),
    );
    const due = billAmountDueOf(row);
    const [advances, entry, approval] = await Promise.all([
      row.status === 'posted' && compareMoney(due, '0') > 0
        ? this.advancesFor(
            tx,
            row.supplierId,
            orderRefs.map((order) => order.id),
          )
        : [],
      row.status === 'posted' ? this.books.entryOf(tx, id, 'purchase_bill') : null,
      this.approvals.history(tx, 'bill', id),
    ]);
    return {
      ...toSummary(row, found.supplier, found.lineCount),
      pricesIncludeVat: row.pricesIncludeVat,
      discount: row.discount,
      warehouseId: row.warehouseId,
      note: row.note,
      lines: billLinesOut,
      expenses: expenses.map((expense) => ({
        id: expense.id,
        accountId: expense.accountId,
        description: expense.description,
        amount: expense.amount,
        taxRate: {
          id: expense.taxRateId,
          name: expense.taxRateName,
          kind: expense.taxRateKind,
          rate: expense.taxRate,
        },
        net: expense.net,
        vat: expense.vat,
        total: expense.total,
      })),
      priceDifference,
      receipts: receiptRefs.map((receipt) => ({ id: receipt.id, number: receipt.number })),
      orders: orderRefs,
      // Posted, so each has a number
      payments: payments.flatMap((payment) =>
        payment.paymentNumber === null
          ? []
          : [{ ...payment, paymentNumber: payment.paymentNumber }],
      ),
      advances,
      entry,
      approval,
    };
  }

  // The supplier's posted payments with money not applied yet (supplier_payments_unapplied_idx):
  // those paid against one of this bill's orders first (decision 12), then the oldest
  private async advancesFor(tx: Transaction, supplierId: string, orderIds: readonly string[]) {
    const rows = await tx
      .select({
        paymentId: supplierPayments.id,
        paymentNumber: supplierPayments.number,
        date: supplierPayments.date,
        amount: supplierPayments.amount,
        applied: supplierPayments.applied,
        orderId: purchaseOrders.id,
        orderNumber: purchaseOrders.number,
      })
      .from(supplierPayments)
      .leftJoin(
        purchaseOrders,
        and(
          eq(purchaseOrders.tenantId, supplierPayments.tenantId),
          eq(purchaseOrders.id, supplierPayments.orderId),
        ),
      )
      .where(
        and(
          eq(supplierPayments.tenantId, getTenantId()),
          eq(supplierPayments.supplierId, supplierId),
          eq(supplierPayments.status, 'posted'),
          sql`${supplierPayments.applied} < ${supplierPayments.amount}`,
        ),
      )
      .orderBy(asc(supplierPayments.date), asc(supplierPayments.id));
    const linked = new Set(orderIds);
    return rows
      .flatMap((row) =>
        row.paymentNumber === null
          ? []
          : [
              {
                paymentId: row.paymentId,
                paymentNumber: row.paymentNumber,
                date: row.date,
                order: row.orderId === null ? null : { id: row.orderId, number: row.orderNumber },
                unapplied: subtractMoney(row.amount, row.applied),
              },
            ],
      )
      .toSorted(
        (a, b) =>
          Number(b.order !== null && linked.has(b.order.id)) -
          Number(a.order !== null && linked.has(a.order.id)),
      );
  }

  private async supplierOf(tx: Transaction, supplierId: string): Promise<PartyRef> {
    const supplier = (await customerRefs(tx, [supplierId])).get(supplierId);
    if (!supplier) throw new Error(`Supplier ${supplierId} is missing`);
    return supplier;
  }

  // What the audit log shows: the header and the size, not every line
  private snapshot(row: BillRow, supplier: PartyRef, fields: CheckedBill) {
    return this.snapshotOf(row, supplier, fields.lines.length, fields.expenses.length);
  }

  private snapshotOf(row: BillRow, supplier: PartyRef, lines: number, expenses: number) {
    return {
      number: row.number,
      date: row.date,
      dueDate: row.dueDate,
      supplier: supplier.code,
      supplierBillNumber: row.supplierBillNumber,
      mushakNumber: row.mushakNumber,
      total: row.total,
      lines,
      expenses,
    };
  }
}

// A goods line of its own as resolveReceiptLines() takes it: everything accepted, nothing rejected
function ownGoodsInput(line: BillLineInput) {
  return {
    variantId: line.variantId,
    unitId: line.unitId,
    quantity: line.quantity,
    serialNumbers: [...line.serialNumbers],
    lotNumber: line.lotNumber,
    expiresOn: line.expiresOn,
    manufacturedOn: line.manufacturedOn,
    orderLineId: null,
    rejectedQuantity: '0',
    rejectionReason: null,
  };
}

// The accounts a service line or an expense posts to (decision 6): an active expense or asset
// ledger (a repair is an expense, a new sewing machine an asset) that is not one only the system
// posts to: no purpose (the payable, VAT, inventory, cost of goods sold), no stock account (goods
// received not billed, goods in transit) and no money account (a payment pays a bill, a bill does
// not). FOR SHARE: nobody archives one before we commit; the posting checks them again.
async function checkCostAccounts(
  tx: Transaction,
  wanted: readonly { path: string; accountId: string }[],
): Promise<void> {
  if (wanted.length === 0) return;
  const tenantId = getTenantId();
  const chart = await tx
    .select({
      id: ledgerAccounts.id,
      parentId: ledgerAccounts.parentId,
      type: ledgerAccounts.type,
      purpose: ledgerAccounts.purpose,
      isGroup: ledgerAccounts.isGroup,
      holdsMoney: ledgerAccounts.holdsMoney,
      archivedAt: ledgerAccounts.archivedAt,
    })
    .from(ledgerAccounts)
    .where(eq(ledgerAccounts.tenantId, tenantId));
  const money = moneyAccountIds(
    chart.map((account) => ({ ...account, archivedAt: account.archivedAt?.toISOString() ?? null })),
  );
  const stock = await stockAccountIds(tx);
  const usable = new Set(
    chart
      .filter(
        (account) =>
          (account.type === 'expense' || account.type === 'asset') &&
          !account.isGroup &&
          account.archivedAt === null &&
          account.purpose === null &&
          !money.has(account.id) &&
          !stock.has(account.id),
      )
      .map((account) => account.id),
  );
  const issues: LineIssue[] = wanted.flatMap((item) =>
    usable.has(item.accountId) ? [] : [{ path: item.path, code: 'bill_account_invalid' }],
  );
  if (issues.length > 0) throw linesError(issues);
  await tx
    .select({ id: ledgerAccounts.id })
    .from(ledgerAccounts)
    .where(
      and(
        eq(ledgerAccounts.tenantId, tenantId),
        inArray(ledgerAccounts.id, [...new Set(wanted.map((item) => item.accountId))]),
      ),
    )
    .for('share');
}
```

The service reads like 15c's invoices with 17b's approval in place of "Post". The parts that differ:

- **`checkSources()`** is the invoice's, for receipt lines and service lines. A receipt line must be on a posted
  receipt of this supplier that a person made (a receipt a bill made has `bill_id`, and is that bill's), of the same
  item, with something accepted, billed whole in any unit (`bill_receipt_line_quantity`), and not billed yet. A
  service line must be a service on an approved, received or closed order of this supplier, the same item, unit and
  quantity, and billed by no other posted bill. Drafts hold nothing (decision 29), so these are checked at save, at
  submit and again at posting.
- **The locks:** a save takes the service lines' orders `FOR SHARE`, so an order is not reopened under it. The posting
  takes the receipt lines and the service lines `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` in id order, the same as 0040's own check: a
  second bill posting the same line waits, then finds it billed. `NO KEY` does not block a draft bill line saved
  against the same line (its foreign key takes only a `KEY SHARE` lock).
- **The price setting:** the orders' when the lines bill orders (17b's decision 15), else the form's. Two orders that
  disagree are `bill_vat_mixed`, like the invoice's `invoice_vat_mixed`.
- **`checkOwnLines()`:** a goods line of its own needs the warehouse and is checked like a goods receipt line now, so
  the person sees "enter the lot" when saving, not at the approval days later. A service line (of its own or from an
  order) gets its account, or Settings' "Purchased services" (decision 38), and takes no lot. Errors of the receipt
  checks are moved onto the bill's own lines with `onBillLines()`, the invoice's trick.
- **`checkCostAccounts()`** is decision 40. It reads the whole chart once, to find the money accounts the way the forms
  do (`moneyAccountIds()`), then locks the chosen accounts `FOR SHARE`.
- **The due date** is decision 39: the shortest payment terms of the orders, else the supplier's.
- **`warehouseId` is stored only with goods of its own;** the contract says null when there are none, and the posting
  reads it as "receive here".
- **`submitLocked()`** checks the bill again as it stands now (`recheck()`: active supplier, branch and warehouse,
  every source, every account), numbers it while it is still a draft (`bills_number_check`) and hands it to the
  engine with its total, VAT included. With no level, the engine posts it in the same request.
- **`postLocked()`** keeps the order 0040 needs: (1) the goods of its own lines come in through `receiveForBill()`,
  (2) each such line gets its new receipt line in an `UPDATE` of that one column (the only change a pending bill's
  line allows), (3) every receipt line is marked billed, `false → true`, and the count must match, (4) the entry,
  (5) posted last, when the database checks (1)–(3). A refused step rolls everything back, the approval with it.
- **`billRace()`** turns the database's last word into the codes the form knows: the supplier number index (two saves
  of one bill at the same moment), and the posting checks (two bills of one line posted at the same moment).
- **`reopen()` and `cancel()`:** a pending bill is reopened through the engine, which ends its round as reopened; a
  cancel of a pending bill reopens it first in the same transaction (decision 31). A posted bill is neither: a debit
  note corrects it (17d).
- **`read()`** sends each line's receipt number, order number, order value (only from a receipt made from an order) and
  what the goods came with: the receipt line's batch once received, else the lot typed on a line of its own. The
  payments are posted payments only: a draft's plan is not money paid. **`advancesFor()`** lists the supplier's
  posted payments with money left, those paid against one of the bill's orders first (decision 12).

### Supplier payments: `purchase/supplier-payments.service.ts` (new)

```ts
import { Inject, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import {
  billAmountDueOf,
  compareMoney,
  overAllocated,
  type PartyRef,
  type SupplierPayment,
  type SupplierPaymentInput,
  type SupplierPaymentStatus,
  type SupplierPaymentSummary,
  sumMoney,
  type UpdateSupplierPaymentInput,
  type VoidSupplierPaymentInput,
} from '@omnivo/contracts';
import {
  bills,
  parties,
  partyBankAccounts,
  purchaseOrders,
  supplierPaymentAllocations,
  supplierPayments,
} from '@omnivo/db';
import { and, asc, desc, eq, inArray, type SQL, sql } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { z } from 'zod';

import { audit, created, diff } from '../common/audit/audit.js';
import { isCheckViolation } from '../common/db/pg-errors.js';
import { AppError, notFound, versionConflict } from '../common/http/app-error.js';
import { decodeCursor, toPage } from '../common/pagination/cursor.js';
import { currentPrincipal, getTenantId } from '../common/tenant/tenant-context.js';
import type { Transaction, WithTenant } from '../common/tenant/with-tenant.js';
import { WITH_TENANT } from '../infra/tokens.js';
import { type LineIssue, linesError } from '../inventory/stock-lines.js';
import { NumberingService } from '../numbering/numbering.service.js';
import { allocationChanges, allocationPath } from '../sales/allocations.js';
import { assertBranch, assertMoneyAccount, customerRefs } from '../sales/sales-lines.js';
import { ApprovalsService } from './approvals.service.js';
import { PurchaseBooksService } from './purchase-books.service.js';
import { assertSupplier } from './purchase-lines.js';

type PaymentRow = typeof supplierPayments.$inferSelect;

const cursorSchema = z.tuple([z.iso.date(), z.uuid()]);

interface Allocation {
  billId: string;
  amount: string;
}

function notDraft(): AppError {
  return new AppError(
    409,
    'purchase_not_draft',
    'This payment was submitted. Reopen it to change it, if it is not posted.',
  );
}

function wasSubmitted(): AppError {
  return new AppError(
    409,
    'purchase_was_submitted',
    'This payment was submitted once, so its number and approval history stay. Cancel it instead.',
  );
}

function notPosted(): AppError {
  return new AppError(
    409,
    'payment_not_posted',
    'Only a posted payment is applied again or voided. Change a draft with its form.',
  );
}

function overAllocatedError(): AppError {
  return new AppError(
    409,
    'payment_over_allocated',
    'More is applied than the payment paid. Lower the amounts on the bills.',
    { fieldErrors: { allocations: ['payment_over_allocated'] } },
  );
}

// The database's last word, if two writers got past the checks below: a bill paid past its total
// (bills_paid_check, two payments posted for its last money at the same moment), a payment applied
// past its amount (supplier_payments_amount_check), or money put on a bill that is not posted
// (supplier_payment_allocations_bill_check)
function paymentRace(error: unknown): unknown {
  if (isCheckViolation(error, 'bills_paid_check')) {
    return new AppError(
      409,
      'payment_over_bill',
      'Another payment paid one of these bills first. Reload and try again.',
    );
  }
  if (isCheckViolation(error, 'supplier_payments_amount_check')) return overAllocatedError();
  if (isCheckViolation(error, 'supplier_payment_allocations_bill_check')) {
    return new AppError(409, 'payment_bill_invalid', 'Pick a posted bill of this supplier.');
  }
  return error;
}

function toSummary(
  row: PaymentRow,
  supplier: PartyRef,
  order: { id: string; number: string | null } | null,
): SupplierPaymentSummary {
  return {
    id: row.id,
    number: row.number,
    date: row.date,
    supplier,
    amount: row.amount,
    applied: row.applied,
    method: row.method,
    reference: row.reference,
    accountId: row.accountId,
    branchId: row.branchId,
    order,
    status: row.status,
    postedAt: row.postedAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
    version: row.version,
    updatedAt: row.updatedAt.toISOString(),
  };
}

// Supplier payments (step 17c): a money receipt the other way round, with the approval in the
// middle (decision 5). A draft's allocations are a plan (decision 23): they are rows, so the form
// and the list show what will be applied, but no bill counts them until the payment is posted. The
// last approval posts it (decision 7): its entry is booked and its plan lands on the bills. A
// posted payment is applied again or voided, never edited.
@Injectable()
export class SupplierPaymentsService {
  constructor(
    @Inject(WITH_TENANT) private readonly withTenant: WithTenant,
    private readonly numbering: NumberingService,
    private readonly approvals: ApprovalsService,
    private readonly books: PurchaseBooksService,
  ) {
    approvals.onApproved('supplier_payment', (tx, id) => this.post(tx, id));
  }

  list(query: {
    limit: number;
    cursor?: string | undefined;
    status?: SupplierPaymentStatus | undefined;
    supplierId?: string | undefined;
    orderId?: string | undefined;
  }): Promise<{ items: SupplierPaymentSummary[]; nextCursor: string | null }> {
    const after = decodeCursor(query.cursor, cursorSchema);
    return this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
      const rows = await this.rows(
        tx,
        and(
          query.status === undefined ? undefined : eq(supplierPayments.status, query.status),
          query.supplierId === undefined
            ? undefined
            : eq(supplierPayments.supplierId, query.supplierId),
          query.orderId === undefined ? undefined : eq(supplierPayments.orderId, query.orderId),
          after === undefined
            ? undefined
            : sql`(${supplierPayments.date}, ${supplierPayments.id}) < (${after[0]}::date, ${after[1]}::uuid)`,
        ),
        query.limit + 1,
      );
      const page = toPage(rows, query.limit, (last) => [last.payment.date, last.payment.id]);
      return {
        items: page.items.map((row) => toSummary(row.payment, row.supplier, row.order)),
        nextCursor: page.nextCursor,
      };
    });
  }

  get(id: string): Promise<SupplierPayment> {
    return this.withTenant((tx) => this.read(tx, id));
  }

  async create(input: SupplierPaymentInput): Promise<SupplierPayment> {
    try {
      return await this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
        const supplier = await assertSupplier(tx, input.supplierId);
        await this.check(tx, supplier.id, input);
        const userId = currentPrincipal().userId;
        const [row] = await tx
          .insert(supplierPayments)
          .values({
            tenantId: getTenantId(),
            ...this.fields(supplier.id, input),
            createdBy: userId,
            updatedBy: userId,
          })
          .returning();
        if (!row) throw new Error('Supplier payment insert returned no row');
        await this.replaceAllocations(tx, row, input.allocations);
        await audit(tx, {
          action: 'supplier_payment.created',
          entityType: 'supplier_payment',
          entityId: row.id,
          changes: created(this.snapshot(row, supplier, input.allocations.length)),
        });
        if (input.submit) await this.submitLocked(tx, row);
        return this.read(tx, row.id);
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw paymentRace(error);
    }
  }

  async update(id: string, input: UpdateSupplierPaymentInput): Promise<SupplierPayment> {
    try {
      return await this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
        const before = await this.lockDraft(tx, id, input.version);
        const planBefore = await this.allocationsOf(tx, id);
        const supplierBefore = await this.supplierOf(tx, before.supplierId);
        const supplier = await assertSupplier(tx, input.supplierId, before.supplierId);
        // Numbered: the approvers saw it as a payment to this supplier
        if (before.number !== null && supplier.id !== before.supplierId) {
          throw new AppError(
            409,
            'purchase_supplier_invalid',
            'This payment was submitted for its supplier. Write a new payment for another one.',
            { fieldErrors: { supplierId: ['purchase_supplier_invalid'] } },
          );
        }
        await this.check(tx, supplier.id, input);
        // The plan first: a new supplier's key would refuse the old supplier's bills
        await this.replaceAllocations(tx, before, []);
        const [updated] = await tx
          .update(supplierPayments)
          .set({
            ...this.fields(supplier.id, input),
            version: sql`${supplierPayments.version} + 1`,
            updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
          })
          .where(and(eq(supplierPayments.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(supplierPayments.id, id)))
          .returning();
        if (!updated) throw notFound('Supplier payment');
        await this.replaceAllocations(tx, updated, input.allocations);
        await audit(tx, {
          action: 'supplier_payment.updated',
          entityType: 'supplier_payment',
          entityId: id,
          changes: diff(
            this.snapshot(before, supplierBefore, planBefore.length),
            this.snapshot(updated, supplier, input.allocations.length),
          ),
        });
        if (input.submit) await this.submitLocked(tx, updated);
        return this.read(tx, id);
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw paymentRace(error);
    }
  }

  // Only a draft that was never submitted; its plan goes with it (ON DELETE CASCADE)
  async remove(id: string, version: number): Promise<void> {
    try {
      await this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
        const before = await this.lockDraft(tx, id, version);
        if (before.number !== null) throw wasSubmitted();
        const plan = await this.allocationsOf(tx, id);
        const supplier = await this.supplierOf(tx, before.supplierId);
        await tx
          .delete(supplierPayments)
          .where(and(eq(supplierPayments.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(supplierPayments.id, id)));
        const snapshot = this.snapshot(before, supplier, plan.length);
        await audit(tx, {
          action: 'supplier_payment.deleted',
          entityType: 'supplier_payment',
          entityId: id,
          changes: diff(
            snapshot,
            Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(snapshot).map((field) => [field, null])),
          ),
        });
      });
    } catch (error) {
      if (isCheckViolation(error, 'supplier_payments_submitted_immutable')) throw wasSubmitted();
      throw error;
    }
  }

  async submit(id: string, version: number): Promise<SupplierPayment> {
    try {
      return await this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
        const row = await this.lockDraft(tx, id, version);
        await this.submitLocked(tx, row);
        return this.read(tx, id);
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw paymentRace(error);
    }
  }

  reopen(id: string, version: number): Promise<SupplierPayment> {
    return this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
      const row = await this.lock(tx, id, version);
      if (row.status !== 'pending') {
        throw new AppError(
          409,
          'purchase_cannot_reopen',
          'Only a payment waiting for approval can be reopened.',
        );
      }
      await this.approvals.reopen(tx, 'supplier_payment', id, 'pending');
      return this.read(tx, id);
    });
  }

  // Will not be paid: a numbered draft, or a pending payment reopened first in the same transaction
  // (decision 31). Its plan stays as history; the database freezes it.
  cancel(id: string, version: number): Promise<SupplierPayment> {
    return this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
      const row = await this.lock(tx, id, version);
      if (row.status !== 'draft' && row.status !== 'pending') {
        throw new AppError(
          409,
          'purchase_cannot_cancel',
          'A posted payment is not cancelled. Void it instead.',
        );
      }
      if (row.number === null) {
        throw new AppError(
          409,
          'purchase_delete_instead',
          'This payment was never submitted. Delete it instead.',
        );
      }
      if (row.status === 'pending') {
        await this.approvals.reopen(tx, 'supplier_payment', id, 'pending');
      }
      await tx
        .update(supplierPayments)
        .set({
          status: 'cancelled',
          version: sql`${supplierPayments.version} + 1`,
          updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
        })
        .where(and(eq(supplierPayments.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(supplierPayments.id, id)));
      await audit(tx, {
        action: 'supplier_payment.cancelled',
        entityType: 'supplier_payment',
        entityId: id,
        changes: diff({ status: row.status }, { status: 'cancelled' }),
      });
      return this.read(tx, id);
    });
  }

  // A posted payment's money on other bills: an advance applied to the bill that came, or moved
  // from one bill to another (decision 23). No approval: the money left already, and only which
  // bill it settles changes. Nothing in the books changes either: the payable is one number per
  // supplier.
  async allocate(
    id: string,
    input: { version: number; allocations: readonly Allocation[] },
  ): Promise<SupplierPayment> {
    try {
      return await this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
        const row = await this.lock(tx, id, input.version);
        if (row.status !== 'posted') throw notPosted();
        if (overAllocated(row.amount, input.allocations)) throw overAllocatedError();
        const before = await this.allocationsOf(tx, id);
        await checkBillAllocations(tx, {
          supplierId: row.supplierId,
          current: before,
          wanted: input.allocations,
        });
        await this.replaceAllocations(tx, row, input.allocations);
        await tx
          .update(supplierPayments)
          .set({
            version: sql`${supplierPayments.version} + 1`,
            updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
          })
          .where(and(eq(supplierPayments.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(supplierPayments.id, id)));
        await audit(tx, {
          action: 'supplier_payment.allocated',
          entityType: 'supplier_payment',
          entityId: id,
          changes: allocationChanges(
            before.map(asInvoiceNumber),
            (await this.allocationsOf(tx, id)).map(asInvoiceNumber),
          ),
        });
        return this.read(tx, id);
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw paymentRace(error);
    }
  }

  // A bounced cheque or a payment typed by mistake: its money comes off the bills, and its entry is
  // reversed on the void date. The payment stays, voided, with its number.
  void(id: string, input: VoidSupplierPaymentInput): Promise<SupplierPayment> {
    return this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
      const row = await this.lock(tx, id, input.version);
      if (row.status !== 'posted') throw notPosted();
      if (input.date < row.date) {
        throw new AppError(
          409,
          'payment_void_date',
          'A payment cannot be voided before the day it was paid.',
          { fieldErrors: { date: ['payment_void_date'] } },
        );
      }
      const entry = await this.books.entryOf(tx, id, 'purchase_payment');
      if (entry === null) throw new Error(`Supplier payment ${id} has no entry`);
      // The allocations first: the database lets a payment be voided only once nothing of it is
      // applied (supplier_payments_void_check). Their trigger takes the money off the bills.
      const before = await this.allocationsOf(tx, id);
      await checkBillAllocations(tx, { supplierId: row.supplierId, current: before, wanted: [] });
      await this.replaceAllocations(tx, row, []);
      await tx
        .update(supplierPayments)
        .set({
          status: 'voided',
          voidDate: input.date,
          voidReason: input.reason,
          version: sql`${supplierPayments.version} + 1`,
          updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
        })
        .where(and(eq(supplierPayments.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(supplierPayments.id, id)));
      const reversal = await this.books.reverse(tx, entry, {
        date: input.date,
        narration: `Payment ${row.number ?? ''} voided: ${input.reason}`,
      });
      await audit(tx, {
        action: 'supplier_payment.voided',
        entityType: 'supplier_payment',
        entityId: id,
        changes: created({ date: input.date, reason: input.reason, reversal: reversal.number }),
      });
      return this.read(tx, id);
    });
  }

  // Numbered the first time, checked again as it stands now, then handed to the engine with its
  // amount. With no level for it, the engine posts it at once (post() below).
  private async submitLocked(tx: Transaction, row: PaymentRow): Promise<void> {
    await this.recheck(tx, row);
    if (row.number === null) {
      await tx
        .update(supplierPayments)
        .set({ number: await this.numbering.next(tx, 'purchase.payment', row.date) })
        .where(and(eq(supplierPayments.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(supplierPayments.id, row.id)));
    }
    await this.approvals.submit(tx, 'supplier_payment', row.id, row.amount);
  }

  // The stored payment against what is true now: an active supplier, branch and money account,
  // and a plan that still fits what each bill owes. The bills are locked (checkBillAllocations),
  // so at posting a second payment for the same bills waits, then sees what this one paid.
  private async recheck(tx: Transaction, row: PaymentRow): Promise<void> {
    await assertSupplier(tx, row.supplierId);
    await assertBranch(tx, row.branchId, 'purchase_branch_invalid');
    await assertMoneyAccount(tx, row.accountId, 'payment_account_invalid');
    // A draft's plan is not on the bills yet, so nothing of it counts as owed again
    await checkBillAllocations(tx, {
      supplierId: row.supplierId,
      current: [],
      wanted: await this.allocationsOf(tx, row.id),
    });
  }

  // Posting (decision 7), called by the approvals engine. The payment is locked and pending, its
  // round approved. The entry first (a closed period refuses there), then the status: posting adds
  // the plan to the bills in one trigger (supplier_payments_post), in bill id order.
  private async post(tx: Transaction, id: string): Promise<void> {
    try {
      const [row] = await tx
        .select()
        .from(supplierPayments)
        .where(and(eq(supplierPayments.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(supplierPayments.id, id)));
      if (row?.status !== 'pending' || row.number === null) {
        throw new Error(`Supplier payment ${id} is not a numbered pending payment`);
      }
      await this.recheck(tx, row);
      const entry = await this.books.payment(
        tx,
        { id, number: row.number, date: row.date },
        {
          supplierId: row.supplierId,
          branchId: row.branchId,
          accountId: row.accountId,
          amount: row.amount,
        },
      );
      await tx
        .update(supplierPayments)
        .set({
          status: 'posted',
          postedAt: new Date(),
          postedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
          version: sql`${supplierPayments.version} + 1`,
          updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
        })
        .where(and(eq(supplierPayments.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(supplierPayments.id, id)));
      await audit(tx, {
        action: 'supplier_payment.posted',
        entityType: 'supplier_payment',
        entityId: id,
        changes: created({ number: row.number, entry: entry.number }),
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw paymentRace(error);
    }
  }

  // Every rule of a save the contract cannot check: the branch, the money account, the supplier's
  // own bank account, the order an advance names, and a plan of the supplier's posted bills that
  // fits what each still owes. The plan holds nothing (decision 23): it is checked again when the
  // payment is submitted and posted.
  private async check(
    tx: Transaction,
    supplierId: string,
    input: SupplierPaymentInput,
  ): Promise<void> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    await assertBranch(tx, input.branchId, 'purchase_branch_invalid');
    await assertMoneyAccount(tx, input.accountId, 'payment_account_invalid');
    if (input.supplierBankAccountId !== null) {
      // FOR SHARE: the supplier's form removing this account waits until we commit (and then the
      // database clears our link, decision 33)
      const [account] = await tx
        .select({ id: partyBankAccounts.id })
        .from(partyBankAccounts)
        .where(
          and(
            eq(partyBankAccounts.tenantId, tenantId),
            eq(partyBankAccounts.id, input.supplierBankAccountId),
            eq(partyBankAccounts.partyId, supplierId),
          ),
        )
        .for('share');
      if (!account) {
        throw new AppError(
          409,
          'payment_bank_account_invalid',
          "Pick one of this supplier's bank accounts.",
          { fieldErrors: { supplierBankAccountId: ['payment_bank_account_invalid'] } },
        );
      }
    }
    if (input.orderId !== null) {
      // An advance is paid against an order the company agreed to (decision 12)
      const [order] = await tx
        .select({ status: purchaseOrders.status })
        .from(purchaseOrders)
        .where(
          and(
            eq(purchaseOrders.tenantId, tenantId),
            eq(purchaseOrders.id, input.orderId),
            eq(purchaseOrders.supplierId, supplierId),
          ),
        );
      if (!order || !['approved', 'received', 'closed'].includes(order.status)) {
        throw new AppError(
          409,
          'payment_order_invalid',
          'Pick an approved purchase order of this supplier.',
          { fieldErrors: { orderId: ['payment_order_invalid'] } },
        );
      }
    }
    await checkBillAllocations(tx, { supplierId, current: [], wanted: input.allocations });
  }

  private fields(supplierId: string, input: SupplierPaymentInput) {
    return {
      date: input.date,
      supplierId,
      amount: input.amount,
      accountId: input.accountId,
      method: input.method,
      reference: input.reference,
      supplierBankAccountId: input.supplierBankAccountId,
      branchId: input.branchId,
      orderId: input.orderId,
      note: input.note,
    };
  }

  // Replaces the payment's rows: a draft's plan on every save, a posted payment's money when it is
  // applied again or voided. amount_paid and applied are not written here: the allocations'
  // trigger keeps them, and moves a bill only for a posted payment (migration 0040).
  private async replaceAllocations(
    tx: Transaction,
    payment: PaymentRow,
    wanted: readonly Allocation[],
  ): Promise<void> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    await tx
      .delete(supplierPaymentAllocations)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(supplierPaymentAllocations.tenantId, tenantId),
          eq(supplierPaymentAllocations.paymentId, payment.id),
        ),
      );
    if (wanted.length === 0) return;
    await tx.insert(supplierPaymentAllocations).values(
      wanted.map((allocation) => ({
        tenantId,
        paymentId: payment.id,
        supplierId: payment.supplierId,
        billId: allocation.billId,
        amount: allocation.amount,
      })),
    );
  }

  // FOR UPDATE: every change to a payment takes turns with the others and with an approval
  private async lock(tx: Transaction, id: string, version: number): Promise<PaymentRow> {
    const [row] = await tx
      .select()
      .from(supplierPayments)
      .where(and(eq(supplierPayments.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(supplierPayments.id, id)))
      .for('update');
    if (!row) throw notFound('Supplier payment');
    if (row.version !== version) throw versionConflict();
    return row;
  }

  private async lockDraft(tx: Transaction, id: string, version: number): Promise<PaymentRow> {
    const row = await this.lock(tx, id, version);
    if (row.status !== 'draft') throw notDraft();
    return row;
  }

  // The bills it pays (or plans to), oldest due date first: the order the form suggested them in
  private allocationsOf(tx: Transaction, paymentId: string) {
    return tx
      .select({
        billId: bills.id,
        billNumber: bills.number,
        supplierBillNumber: bills.supplierBillNumber,
        billDate: bills.date,
        dueDate: bills.dueDate,
        billTotal: bills.total,
        amount: supplierPaymentAllocations.amount,
      })
      .from(supplierPaymentAllocations)
      .innerJoin(
        bills,
        and(
          eq(bills.tenantId, supplierPaymentAllocations.tenantId),
          eq(bills.id, supplierPaymentAllocations.billId),
        ),
      )
      .where(
        and(
          eq(supplierPaymentAllocations.tenantId, getTenantId()),
          eq(supplierPaymentAllocations.paymentId, paymentId),
        ),
      )
      .orderBy(asc(bills.dueDate), asc(bills.id));
  }

  private rows(tx: Transaction, where: SQL | undefined, limit: number) {
    return tx
      .select({
        payment: supplierPayments,
        supplier: { id: parties.id, code: parties.code, name: parties.name },
        order: { id: purchaseOrders.id, number: purchaseOrders.number },
      })
      .from(supplierPayments)
      .innerJoin(
        parties,
        and(
          eq(parties.tenantId, supplierPayments.tenantId),
          eq(parties.id, supplierPayments.supplierId),
        ),
      )
      .leftJoin(
        purchaseOrders,
        and(
          eq(purchaseOrders.tenantId, supplierPayments.tenantId),
          eq(purchaseOrders.id, supplierPayments.orderId),
        ),
      )
      .where(and(eq(supplierPayments.tenantId, getTenantId()), where))
      .orderBy(desc(supplierPayments.date), desc(supplierPayments.id))
      .limit(limit);
  }

  private async read(tx: Transaction, id: string): Promise<SupplierPayment> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    const [found] = await this.rows(tx, eq(supplierPayments.id, id), 1);
    if (!found) throw notFound('Supplier payment');
    const { payment: row } = found;
    const [allocations, bankAccount, entry, approval] = await Promise.all([
      this.allocationsOf(tx, id),
      row.supplierBankAccountId === null
        ? []
        : tx
            .select({
              id: partyBankAccounts.id,
              bankName: partyBankAccounts.bankName,
              branchName: partyBankAccounts.branchName,
              accountName: partyBankAccounts.accountName,
              accountNumber: partyBankAccounts.accountNumber,
              routingNumber: partyBankAccounts.routingNumber,
            })
            .from(partyBankAccounts)
            .where(
              and(
                eq(partyBankAccounts.tenantId, tenantId),
                eq(partyBankAccounts.id, row.supplierBankAccountId),
              ),
            ),
      row.status === 'posted' || row.status === 'voided'
        ? this.books.entryOf(tx, id, 'purchase_payment')
        : null,
      this.approvals.history(tx, 'supplier_payment', id),
    ]);
    const voidEntry =
      row.status === 'voided' && entry !== null ? await this.books.reversalOf(tx, entry.id) : null;
    return {
      ...toSummary(row, found.supplier, found.order),
      note: row.note,
      supplierBankAccount: bankAccount[0] ?? null,
      // Money is applied only to posted bills, so each has a number
      allocations: allocations.flatMap((allocation) =>
        allocation.billNumber === null
          ? []
          : [{ ...allocation, billNumber: allocation.billNumber }],
      ),
      entry,
      voidEntry,
      voidDate: row.voidDate,
      voidReason: row.voidReason,
      approval,
    };
  }

  private async supplierOf(tx: Transaction, supplierId: string): Promise<PartyRef> {
    const supplier = (await customerRefs(tx, [supplierId])).get(supplierId);
    if (!supplier) throw new Error(`Supplier ${supplierId} is missing`);
    return supplier;
  }

  // What the audit log shows
  private snapshot(row: PaymentRow, supplier: PartyRef, bills: number) {
    return {
      number: row.number,
      date: row.date,
      supplier: supplier.code,
      amount: row.amount,
      method: row.method,
      reference: row.reference,
      bills,
    };
  }
}

// allocationChanges() (step 15c) names each row by its invoice number; a bill's number takes that
// place in the audit log
function asInvoiceNumber(allocation: { billNumber: string | null; amount: string }) {
  return { invoiceNumber: allocation.billNumber, amount: allocation.amount };
}

// Checks `wanted` before it replaces `current` (the payment's rows that bills count now: a posted
// payment's; a draft's plan counts on no bill, so it passes none). Every bill of both lists is
// locked FOR NO KEY UPDATE in id order before anything is read, like the invoices of a receipt
// (allocations.ts): two payments for one bill take turns, and the second sees what the first paid.
// Each wanted row must name a posted bill of the supplier and fit what it still owes, where this
// payment's own current row counts as owed again. All problems at once, each under its row.
async function checkBillAllocations(
  tx: Transaction,
  input: {
    supplierId: string;
    current: readonly Allocation[];
    wanted: readonly Allocation[];
  },
): Promise<void> {
  const billIds = [
    ...new Set([...input.current, ...input.wanted].map((allocation) => allocation.billId)),
  ];
  const rows =
    billIds.length === 0
      ? []
      : await tx
          .select({
            id: bills.id,
            supplierId: bills.supplierId,
            status: bills.status,
            total: bills.total,
            amountPaid: bills.amountPaid,
          })
          .from(bills)
          .where(and(eq(bills.tenantId, getTenantId()), inArray(bills.id, billIds)))
          .orderBy(asc(bills.id))
          .for('no key update');
  const byId = new Map(rows.map((row) => [row.id, row]));
  const had = new Map(input.current.map((allocation) => [allocation.billId, allocation.amount]));
  const issues: LineIssue[] = [];
  input.wanted.forEach((allocation, index) => {
    const bill = byId.get(allocation.billId);
    if (bill?.supplierId !== input.supplierId || bill.status !== 'posted') {
      issues.push({ path: allocationPath(index, 'billId'), code: 'payment_bill_invalid' });
      return;
    }
    const due = sumMoney([billAmountDueOf(bill), had.get(allocation.billId) ?? '0']);
    if (compareMoney(allocation.amount, due) > 0) {
      issues.push({ path: allocationPath(index, 'amount'), code: 'payment_over_bill' });
    }
  });
  if (issues.length > 0) throw linesError(issues);
}
```

The service reads like 15c's money receipts with the approval in the middle. The parts that differ:

- **The plan is rows** (decisions 23 and 32): a draft's allocations are written on every save with
  `replaceAllocations()`, and 0040's trigger moves only `applied`. `update()` empties the plan before it changes the
  header: the rows carry the supplier, so a new supplier would refuse the old supplier's bills.
- **`check()`:** the branch, a money account (`payment_account_invalid`), one of this supplier's bank accounts
  (decision 24, `FOR SHARE` so the supplier's form waits), an approved, received or closed order for an advance
  (decision 44), and the plan against what each bill still owes.
- **`checkBillAllocations()`** is 15c's `checkAllocations()` for bills: every bill of both lists locked `FOR NO KEY
  UPDATE` in id order, each row a posted bill of the supplier, never more than it still owes. `current` is what the
  bills count now: a posted payment's rows when it is applied again, nothing for a draft's plan, which no bill
  counts.
- **`post()`** checks the plan again under those locks, books Dr payable / Cr the money account, then sets the
  status. Posting adds the plan to the bills in one trigger, in bill id order; two payments for the last ৳115 of one
  bill take turns, and the second fails on `bills_paid_check`, which `paymentRace()` turns into `payment_over_bill`.
- **`allocate()` and `void()`** need a posted payment (`payment_not_posted`): a draft's plan is changed with its form.
  Voiding removes the allocations first (the database lets a payment be voided only once nothing of it is applied),
  then sets the status, then reverses the entry on the void date.
- **The audit log of an allocation** reuses `allocationChanges()` of 15c, with the bill's number where the invoice's
  number goes.

## 17c.4 — `apps/api`: the tests

This part adds three test files, all in `apps/api/src/purchase/`. Like every integration test since step 5, they run
against a real Postgres and the real worker:

- `bills.int.spec.ts` follows a knitwear factory's accountant through a month of bills: the mill's bill for fabric
  that came in at two stores and for the carriage on its order, at a price that differs from the order's; the
  dyeing house's bill for its work; a thread shop's bill with no order, which receives its own goods; the landlord's
  rent, rejected once and typed again. The approval, the posting, the goods receipts' and orders' "billed" counts,
  Settings → Purchase, two bills of one delivery at the same moment, and what a posted bill keeps from being deleted.
- `supplier-payments.int.spec.ts` follows a denim factory's cashier: a cheque that pays the oldest bills first, a plan
  that no longer fits when it is submitted, an advance against an order that is applied when the bill comes, a
  cheque that bounces, a payment that is taken back and cancelled, and two transfers for one bill's last money.
- `bills.tenant-leak.int.spec.ts`: workspace A must never see, change, approve, pay or apply money to anything of
  workspace B's, nor bill B's receipts or order lines, post to B's accounts or pay from B's money.

They are also the first time 17c's code ran against a real database. They found two things in 17c.3's code, both
fixed there (the 17c.3 sections above already show the fixed code):

```ts
    const amounts: Amount[] = [
      ...input.goods.flatMap((line) => [
        {
          accountId: accounts.receivedNotBilled(),
          branchId: line.receiptBranchId,
          partyId: null,
          amount: line.orderValue,
        },
        // Only a line that differs needs the account: a bill at the order's prices (or of its own
        // goods only) posts with none chosen
        ...(isZeroMoney(line.difference)
          ? []
          : [
              {
                accountId: accounts.priceDifference(),
                branchId: input.branchId,
                partyId: null,
                amount: line.difference,
              },
            ]),
      ]),
```

- **A bill with no price difference asked for the price difference account anyway.** `bill()` added an amount for the
  difference of every goods line, ৳0 included, and `summed()` dropped the ৳0 only later. Asking for the account
  throws when there is none to use, so the thread shop's bill (its own goods, nothing to differ from) failed with
  `purchase_account_invalid` whenever no account was needed at all. Now a line adds the amount only when it differs.

```ts
        // The same four decimals as a sum of the database's quantities
        billedQuantity: billed.get(line.id) ?? '0.0000',
```

- **An order line no bill billed showed `'0'`,** while a billed one showed `'1000.0000'` and `receivedQuantity`
  always has four decimals. A screen that compares the two strings, or a test that reads them, would trip on it.

One older test changed, below: the number series list has the payment's series now. The other older suites learned
17c's rules in 17c.3 (the approval rules list, the accountant's permissions).

```ts
function send(
  method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE',
  url: string,
  payload?: object,
  as = owner,
) {
  return app.inject({
    method,
    url,
    headers: bearer(as.accessToken),
    ...(payload && { payload }),
  });
}

function problemOf(res: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof send>>) {
  return problemSchema.parse(res.json());
}

function unitId(code: string): string {
  const found = units.find((unit) => unit.code === code);
  if (!found) throw new Error(`no unit ${code}`);
  return found.id;
}

function rateId(name: string): string {
  const found = rates.find((rate) => rate.name === name);
  if (!found) throw new Error(`no VAT rate ${name}`);
  return found.id;
}

function accountId(code: string): string {
  const found = accounts.find((item) => item.code === code);
  if (!found) throw new Error(`no account ${code}`);
  return found.id;
}

function codeOf(id: string | null): string | null {
  if (id === null) return null;
  const found = accounts.find((item) => item.id === id);
  if (!found) throw new Error(`no account ${id}`);
  return found.code;
}

function variantOf(product: Product): string {
  const [variant] = product.variants;
  if (!variant) throw new Error(`${product.name} has no variant`);
  return variant.id;
}

function orderLineOf(order: PurchaseOrder, product: Product): string {
  const found = order.lines.find((line) => line.variantId === variantOf(product));
  if (!found) throw new Error(`no ${product.name} on ${order.number ?? 'the order'}`);
  return found.id;
}

function receiptLineOf(receipt: GoodsReceipt, product: Product) {
  const found = receipt.lines.find((line) => line.variantId === variantOf(product));
  if (!found) throw new Error(`no ${product.name} on ${receipt.number ?? 'the receipt'}`);
  return found;
}

// A user who signs up for a workspace of their own, then joins this one with one role
async function member(
  email: string,
  fullName: string,
  password: string,
  role: Role,
): Promise<SignedIn> {
  await signUp(app, {
    companyName: `${fullName} Trading`,
    workspaceSlug: email.split('@')[0] ?? 'trading',
    fullName,
    email,
    password,
  });
  await joinWithoutRoles(pg.superuserUrl, { email, workspace: 'rupsha-knit' });
  const { items } = memberPageSchema.parse((await send('GET', '/members?limit=50')).json());
  const found = items.find((item) => item.email === email);
  if (!found) throw new Error(`${email} is not a member`);
  const assigned = await send('PUT', `/members/${found.membershipId}/roles`, {
    roleIds: [role.id],
    version: found.version,
  });
  expect(assigned.statusCode, assigned.body).toBe(200);
  return logIn(app, { workspace: 'rupsha-knit', email, password, keepSignedIn: false });
}

// Written and submitted by the Owner: with no order levels, approved at once
async function approvedOrder(
  supplier: Supplier,
  lines: PurchaseOrderLineFormValues[],
  extra: Partial<PurchaseOrderFormValues> = {},
): Promise<PurchaseOrder> {
  const made = await send('POST', '/purchase-orders', {
    supplierId: supplier.id,
    date: '2026-10-12',
    expectedDate: '',
    warehouseId: main.id,
    supplierReference: '',
    paymentTermsDays: 30,
    pricesIncludeVat: false,
    note: '',
    lines,
    ...extra,
  });
  expect(made.statusCode, made.body).toBe(201);
  const draft = purchaseOrderSchema.parse(made.json());
  const res = await send('POST', `/purchase-orders/${draft.id}/submit`, {
    version: draft.version,
  });

  const order = purchaseOrderSchema.parse(res.json());
  expect(order.status).toBe('approved');
  return order;

// A bill line as the form sends it: 15% VAT, no discount, nothing it bills, no account, no lot
function billLine(
  product: Product,
  quantity: string,
  unitPrice: string,
  extra: Partial<BillLineFormValues> = {},
): BillLineFormValues {
  return {
    variantId: variantOf(product),
    unitId: product.baseUnitId,
    quantity,
    description: '',
    unitPrice,
    discountType: 'percent',
    discount: '',
    taxRateId: rateId('VAT 15%'),
    receiptLineId: '',
    orderLineId: '',
    accountId: '',
    lotNumber: '',
    expiresOn: '',
    manufacturedOn: '',
    serialNumbers: [],
    ...extra,
  };
}

// A goods receipt line on the bill, as "Add from goods receipts" fills it: the receipt's unit and
// quantity, the price the person types
function receiptBillLine(
  receipt: GoodsReceipt,
  product: Product,
  unitPrice: string,
  extra: Partial<BillLineFormValues> = {},
): BillLineFormValues {
  const line = receiptLineOf(receipt, product);
  return billLine(product, line.quantity, unitPrice, {
    unitId: line.unitId,
    receiptLineId: line.id,
    ...extra,
  });
}

// An order's service line on the bill: its unit, quantity and price
function serviceBillLine(
  order: PurchaseOrder,
  product: Product,
  extra: Partial<BillLineFormValues> = {},
): BillLineFormValues {
  const line = order.lines.find((item) => item.variantId === variantOf(product));
  if (!line) throw new Error(`no ${product.name} on ${order.number ?? 'the order'}`);
  return billLine(product, line.quantity, line.unitPrice, {
    unitId: line.unitId,
    orderLineId: line.id,
    taxRateId: line.taxRate.id,
    ...extra,
  });
}

function expense(code: string, description: string, amount: string, rate = 'VAT 15%') {
  return { accountId: accountId(code), description, amount, taxRateId: rateId(rate) };
}

function billForm(
  supplier: Supplier,
  lines: BillLineFormValues[],
  extra: Partial<BillFormValues> = {},
): Omit<BillFormValues, 'version'> {
  return {
    supplierId: supplier.id,
    date: '2026-10-16',
    dueDate: '',
    supplierBillNumber: '',
    mushakNumber: '',
    mushakDate: '',
    branchId: main.branchId,
    warehouseId: '',
    pricesIncludeVat: false,
    note: '',
    lines,
    expenses: [],
    submit: false,
    ...extra,
  };
}

// The edit form from a saved bill, as the edit page fills it. The API sends amounts with 4
// decimals; the boxes take 2. A stored receipt line keeps a copy of its order line, which the form
// does not send back (bill_line_source).
function formOf(bill: Bill, extra: Partial<BillFormValues> = {}): BillFormValues {
  const two = (value: string) => value.replace(/(\.\d{2})\d*$/, '$1');
  return {
    supplierId: bill.supplier.id,
    date: bill.date,
    dueDate: bill.dueDate,
    supplierBillNumber: bill.supplierBillNumber,
    mushakNumber: bill.mushakNumber ?? '',
    mushakDate: bill.mushakDate ?? '',
    branchId: bill.branchId,
    warehouseId: bill.warehouseId ?? '',
    pricesIncludeVat: bill.pricesIncludeVat,
    note: bill.note ?? '',
    lines: bill.lines.map((line) => ({
      variantId: line.variantId,
      unitId: line.unitId,
      quantity: line.quantity,
      description: line.description,
      unitPrice: line.unitPrice,
      discountType: line.discountType,
      discount: two(line.discount),
      taxRateId: line.taxRate.id,
      receiptLineId: line.receiptLineId ?? '',
      orderLineId: line.receiptLineId === null ? (line.orderLineId ?? '') : '',
      accountId: line.accountId ?? '',
      lotNumber: line.lotNumber ?? '',
      expiresOn: line.expiresOn ?? '',
      manufacturedOn: line.manufacturedOn ?? '',
      serialNumbers: line.serialNumbers,
    })),
    expenses: bill.expenses.map((item) => ({
      accountId: item.accountId,
      description: item.description,
      amount: two(item.amount),
      taxRateId: item.taxRate.id,
    })),
    submit: false,
    version: bill.version,
    ...extra,
  };
}

// A bill action that takes the version: submit, reopen, cancel
function act(action: 'submit' | 'reopen' | 'cancel', bill: Bill, as = shirin) {
  return send('POST', `/bills/${bill.id}/${action}`, { version: bill.version }, as);
}

async function acted(action: 'submit' | 'reopen' | 'cancel', bill: Bill, as = shirin) {
  const res = await act(action, bill, as);
  expect(res.statusCode, res.body).toBe(200);
  return billSchema.parse(res.json());
}

// Approve or reject the round the bill page showed
function decide(bill: Bill, decision: 'approve' | 'reject', comment = '', as = kamal) {
  const [round] = bill.approval.rounds;
  if (!round) throw new Error(`${bill.number ?? 'the bill'} has no round`);
  return send('POST', `/approvals/bill/${bill.id}/${decision}`, { roundId: round.id, comment }, as);
}

// A journal entry as [account code, debit, credit, branch code] rows, sorted: summed per account
// and branch, the entry's own order is not the point
async function entryLines(id: string | undefined) {
  const entry = journalEntrySchema.parse(
    (await send('GET', `/journal-entries/${id ?? 'none'}`)).json(),
  );
  return entry.lines
    .map((item) => [
      codeOf(item.accountId),
      item.debit,
      item.credit,
      item.branchId === ashulia.branchId ? 'ASH' : 'HO',
    ])
    .toSorted(
      (a, b) =>
        String(a[0]).localeCompare(String(b[0])) || String(a[3]).localeCompare(String(b[3])),
    );
}

// The bill form's "Add from goods receipts" list for a supplier: [number, bill state]
async function toBill(supplier: Supplier) {
  const page = goodsReceiptPageSchema.parse(
    (await send('GET', `/goods-receipts?bill=to_bill&supplierId=${supplier.id}`)).json(),
  );
  return page.items.map((item) => [item.number, item.billState]);
}

// The orders with a service line still to bill, for a supplier
async function servicesToBill(supplier: Supplier) {
  const page = purchaseOrderPageSchema.parse(
    (await send('GET', `/purchase-orders?bill=to_bill&supplierId=${supplier.id}`)).json(),
  );
  return page.items.map((item) => item.number);
}

async function superuserSql<T>(fn: (sql: postgres.Sql) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  const sql = postgres(pg.superuserUrl, { max: 1, onnotice: () => undefined });
  try {
    return await fn(sql);
  } finally {
    await sql.end();
  }
}
```
